pool.text: Spanish missionaries began their conversion efforts of the native communities around this time.
Juan de la Cueva took office as the first mayor of the location.
The Dolores Church was constructed as one of the first important buildings.
The mining town officially became a real villa under the rule of Alonso Fernández.
The San Miguel Cathedral was constructed as an important early building.
The Casa de la Moneda was constructed as one of the early important buildings.
The first Congress declared that two important cities would alternate as capital.
A new constitution established the sister cities as a single Central District.
Missionaries representing the Southern Baptist Convention arrived in the city.
The Church of God of Cleveland, Tennessee, was established in the city.
The International Church of the Foursquare Gospel was established in the city.
The Christian Love Brigade Association arrived to establish a local presence.
Manufacturing assembly plants known as maquiladoras were introduced into the country.
Hurricane Mitch devastated the capital and the rest of the country.
Numerous public health care establishments operated across the Central District.
Residents were estimated to suffer from physical or mental disabilities at given rates.
The city government reported massive revenues exceeding other Central American capitals.
International retail and entertainment arrived with the opening of a new cinema.
Members of a prominent religious movement opened a new temple building.
Honduras ruled out Toncontín airport while another facility opened nearby.
